Automation glossary

The words of industrial automation explained simply: GRAFCET, Ladder, variables, timers, counters. Each term is defined in a few sentences, with a diagram when it helps.

​
Search for a term
All
General concepts
GRAFCET
Ladder
Ladder: time, counting and calculation

68 terms

Action

GRAFCET

A rectangle attached to a step: what the system does while the step is active, such as turning an output on.

An action can be continuous, stored (Set / Reset), conditional, delayed or time-limited.

See also : Step, Stored action, Output

AND

General concepts

Also called : in series

An operator that is true only if all its conditions are true.

In Ladder, AND corresponds to contacts in series.

See also : OR, NOT, Contacts in series and in parallel

AND divergence

GRAFCET

Also called : simultaneous sequences, parallelism

A point where the sequence splits into several branches that all start at the same time and then evolve independently.

A single transition above the double bar crosses it.

See also : OR divergence, Convergence

Branch

GRAFCET

One of the sequences starting from a divergence.

See also : Divergence and convergence

Coil

Ladder

Also called : output coil

A symbol at the end of a network that writes a variable: it takes the value of the contact path before it.

It is used to drive an output or an internal memory.

See also : Contact, Network, Output

Contact

Ladder

Also called : NO contact, NC contact

A symbol that reads a variable. An NO contact (normally open) conducts when its variable is true; an NC contact (normally closed) conducts when it is false.

The contact reflects the behaviour wanted in the program, not the physical wiring of the button.

See also : Coil, Wiring: normally open (NO) and normally closed (NC), Contacts in series and in parallel

Contactor

General concepts

A power switch driven by a coil: it lets a low-power output control a motor or a large load.

See also : Output

Contacts in series and in parallel

Ladder

Also called : in series, in parallel

Contacts in series (one after the other) form an AND; contacts in parallel (on two paths) form an OR.

See also : AND, OR

Convergence

GRAFCET

A point where branches join back. In AND, the sequence continues only once all branches have arrived; in OR, as soon as one branch arrives.

See also : Divergence and convergence, Branch

Conversion

Ladder: time, counting and calculation

Also called : widening, narrowing, *_TO_*

Changing the type of a value. A widening (INT to DINT) is safe; a narrowing (REAL to INT) can lose information and must be requested explicitly.

See also : Type

Counter

Ladder: time, counting and calculation

Also called : CTU, CTD, CTUD, counting up, counting down

A block that counts rising edges. CTU increments on CU, CTD decrements on CD (with LD to load the PV value), CTUD does both. The current value is on the CV pin.

See also : Preset value, Function block, Rising edge

Directed link

GRAFCET

A line joining steps and transitions, read from top to bottom. An arrow is drawn only when it goes back up.

See also : Step, Transition

Divergence and convergence

GRAFCET

Also called : junction, bar

A divergence splits a sequence into several branches, a convergence joins them back. A single bar means OR, a double bar means AND.

See also : OR divergence, AND divergence, Convergence, Branch

Double coil

Ladder

A common mistake: writing the same variable with two coils. Only the last network executed counts, which hides the first.

See also : Network, Execution order

Edge

General concepts

The precise moment a signal changes value: rising edge (false to true) or falling edge (true to false).

An edge lasts a single cycle: it is used to react only once to a press.

See also : Rising edge, Falling edge, Edge contacts P and N

Edge contacts P and N

Ladder

Also called : P contact, N contact, rising edge, falling edge

A P contact conducts for a single cycle, on the rising edge of its variable; an N contact does so on the falling edge.

They are used to react only once to a press.

See also : Edge, Rising edge, Falling edge

Evolution

GRAFCET

Also called : crossing, crossing a transition, firing

Crossing a transition: when the upstream step is active and the receptivity is true, the upstream step deactivates and the downstream step activates.

The upstream step must be active AND the receptivity true: if either is missing, nothing moves.

See also : Transition, Upstream, downstream

Exclusivity

GRAFCET

Also called : mutual exclusion

A property of the branches of an OR divergence whose receptivities cannot be true at the same time.

Without exclusivity, several branches can start at once: the Studomate analysis flags it.

See also : OR divergence

Execution order

General concepts

The rule for reading the program: networks run from top to bottom, and GRAFCETs run before Ladder.

A network placed lower already sees the result of the networks above it within the same cycle. If two networks write the same variable, the last one executed wins.

See also : Scan cycle

Falling edge

General concepts

A signal going from true to false, detected during a single cycle.

See also : Edge, Rising edge

Function block

Ladder: time, counting and calculation

Also called : block

A Ladder rectangle that performs a ready-made function (timing, counting, calculation) from input pins on the left and output pins on the right.

See also : Timer, Counter, Instance

Hysteresis

Ladder: time, counting and calculation

A gap between the switch-on threshold and the switch-off threshold, to prevent an output from flickering when the measurement oscillates around one value.

See also : Scaling

Initial step

GRAFCET

A step with a double outline, active at power-up or after a reset. A GRAFCET has at least one.

See also : Step, Reset

Input

General concepts

A variable read by the program and driven by the outside world: button, switch, sensor.

In the program, an input is read with a contact. The program cannot write it.

See also : Output, Push button, Switch, Wiring: normally open (NO) and normally closed (NC)

Instance

Ladder: time, counting and calculation

One copy of a function block, with its own state: two TON timers are two independent instances.

See also : Function block, Timer, Counter

Interlock

Ladder

Also called : mutual interlock

A condition that forbids two outputs from being active at the same time, like the two directions of a motor: each can start only if the other is off.

See also : Self-holding

Internal memory

Ladder

Also called : memory, memory bit

A variable that is neither an input nor an output: the program uses it to remember a state between two cycles.

See also : Variable, S and R coils, Retentive memory

Ladder

Ladder

Also called : LD, ladder diagram, relay diagram

A graphical PLC programming language: contacts on the left (the conditions) drive a coil on the right (the action).

It descends from the relay diagram and is written « LD » in the IEC 61131-3 standard.

See also : Network, Contact, Coil

Limit switch

General concepts

Also called : end stop

A sensor operated mechanically when a moving part (gate, cylinder) reaches the end of its travel.

See also : Input

Main

Ladder: time, counting and calculation

Also called : main program

The main program of a project, run on every cycle. It calls the subprograms and cannot be excluded from execution.

See also : Subprogram

Mnemonic

General concepts

Also called : variable name

The short, meaningful name of a variable (pump, stop), which programs use to refer to it. An address (%I0.1) can be added to link the variable to physical hardware.

See also : Variable

Network

Ladder

Also called : rung, section

A block of the Ladder program, bounded by its two rails. It contains lines of contacts leading to coils. In the simplest case, a single line: contacts on the left, a coil on the right. It is read from left to right.

If the contact path of a line lets current through, the coil is activated.

See also : Contact, Coil, Execution order

NOT

General concepts

Also called : inversion

An operator that inverts a condition: true becomes false, false becomes true.

In Ladder, NOT corresponds to an NC contact.

See also : AND, OR

OR

General concepts

Also called : in parallel

An operator that is true as soon as one of its conditions is true.

In Ladder, OR corresponds to contacts in parallel.

See also : AND, NOT, Contacts in series and in parallel

OR divergence

GRAFCET

Also called : sequence selection

A point where the sequence splits into several paths of which only one is taken, depending on which receptivity becomes true first.

The branch receptivities must be mutually exclusive.

See also : AND divergence, Exclusivity, Divergence and convergence

Output

General concepts

A variable written by the program to drive a lamp, a contactor, a valve or a motor.

In Ladder an output is driven by a coil; in GRAFCET, by an action.

See also : Input, Contactor

Overflow

Ladder: time, counting and calculation

Also called : wrap-around

A result that goes out of the range of its type: an INT passing 32767 wraps around to the low bound.

See also : Type

PLC

General concepts

Also called : programmable logic controller, programmable controller

A small industrial computer that reads inputs (buttons, sensors), runs a program, then drives outputs (lamps, contactors, valves).

It endlessly repeats the same loop, the scan cycle. In Studomate, the program is written in GRAFCET and Ladder.

See also : Scan cycle, Input, Output

Preset value

Ladder: time, counting and calculation

Also called : PV, preset

The target value of a counter (PV pin). The Q output of a CTU becomes true when the count CV reaches PV.

See also : Counter

Push button

General concepts

A control device that changes state while pressed and returns to rest by itself when released.

See also : Switch, Wiring: normally open (NO) and normally closed (NC), Input

Rails

Ladder

Also called : left rail, right rail

The two vertical lines framing a Ladder network: the notional current flows from the left rail to the right rail.

See also : Network

Receptivity

GRAFCET

Also called : transition condition

The crossing condition of a transition: a true-or-false expression, such as end1 or cycle_start AND NOT stop.

A receptivity can contain a timer or an edge.

See also : Transition, Evolution

Reset

GRAFCET

Also called : reinitialize, GRAFCET reset

Put the whole GRAFCET back in its starting state: all steps inactive except the initial step, which becomes active again.

See also : Initial step

Retentive memory

Ladder

Also called : retentivity

A memory that keeps its value after a power loss or a restart, unlike an ordinary memory that restarts at 0.

See also : S and R coils, Internal memory

Rising edge

General concepts

A signal going from false to true, detected during a single cycle.

See also : Edge, Falling edge

S and R coils

Ladder

Also called : Set, Reset, latch, set to 1, set to 0

An S (Set) coil sets its variable to 1 and leaves it; an R (Reset) coil sets it back to 0. Between orders, the variable keeps its value.

The last network executed wins if both are active together.

See also : Internal memory, Self-holding, Retentive memory

Scaling

Ladder: time, counting and calculation

Also called : raw value

A calculation that converts the raw value of an analog sensor into a physical quantity (temperature, level), usually through a straight line.

See also : Type

Scan cycle

General concepts

Also called : PLC cycle, scan

The loop a PLC repeats endlessly, in three phases: read the inputs, run the program, write the outputs.

A cycle lasts a few milliseconds. While the program runs, inputs are frozen: they keep the value read at the start of the cycle.

See also : PLC, Execution order

Self-holding

Ladder

Also called : latching, seal-in

A circuit where a contact of the coil itself is placed in parallel with the start button: the output stays on after the button is released.

With the stop in series after the parallel, the stop has priority.

See also : Stop priority, S and R coils, Internal memory

Step

GRAFCET

A numbered square representing a stable state of the system. It is active or inactive; an active step is shown with a coloured background in the editor.

The Xn variable of a step is TRUE while step n is active.

See also : Initial step, Action, Transition, Step variable (Xn)

Step variable (Xn)

GRAFCET

Also called : Xn, X2

A logic variable tied to step n: it is TRUE when the step is active (X2 = TRUE).

It is used in a receptivity or in a Ladder program to know where the sequence stands.

See also : Step

Stop priority

Ladder

Also called : start priority

A self-holding circuit where the stop wins if start and stop are operated together. Priority depends on the order of the contacts.

See also : Self-holding

Stored action

GRAFCET

Also called : Set, Reset, Set action

An action whose variable stays true when the step deactivates, until another action sets it back to false (Reset).

See also : Action, S and R coils

Subprogram

Ladder: time, counting and calculation

Also called : subprogram call

A program called from another one through a call block. It lets a project be split into readable, reusable parts.

See also : Main, Function block

Switch

General concepts

Also called : maintained switch, toggle switch

A control device that keeps its position after being operated: it stays on until switched back.

See also : Push button, Wiring: normally open (NO) and normally closed (NC), Input

System time bases

Ladder: time, counting and calculation

Also called : _SYS_TB, system clock

Read-only variables provided by Studomate (prefix _SYS_) that alternate between true and false at a fixed rate, from 200 ms to 2 s, for example to blink a lamp.

See also : Timer

Timer

Ladder: time, counting and calculation

Also called : timer block

A block that measures a duration. It receives an input IN and a duration PT (the preset time), and its output Q responds according to the type: TON, TOF or TP.

See also : TON, TOF, TP, System time bases

Timing diagram

General concepts

Also called : chronogram

A chart showing how several signals change over time, stacked on the same time axis.

See also : Scan cycle

TOF

Ladder: time, counting and calculation

Also called : off-delay timer

Off-delay timer: Q becomes true as soon as IN is true and stays true for the duration PT after IN has fallen.

See also : Timer, TON, TP

Toggle circuit

Ladder

Also called : latching relay, flip-flop

A circuit where each press of a button inverts the state of an output: one press turns it on, the next turns it off.

See also : Edge contacts P and N, S and R coils

TON

Ladder: time, counting and calculation

Also called : on-delay timer

On-delay timer: output Q becomes true when IN has stayed true for the whole duration PT, and falls as soon as IN falls.

See also : Timer, TOF, TP

TP

Ladder: time, counting and calculation

Also called : pulse timer

Pulse timer: a rising edge on IN triggers an output Q that is true for exactly the duration PT, whatever IN does afterwards.

See also : Timer, TON, TOF

Transition

GRAFCET

A small horizontal bar linking two steps and carrying a receptivity: the condition to meet to go from one to the other.

See also : Receptivity, Evolution, Step

Truth table

General concepts

A table giving the value of a logic expression for every combination of its variables (0 = false, 1 = true).

See also : AND, OR, NOT

Type

Ladder: time, counting and calculation

Also called : BOOL, INT, DINT, REAL, variable type

The nature of a variable's value: BOOL (true or false), INT and DINT (16-bit and 32-bit integers), REAL (floating-point number).

Each type has its own range of values and calculation rules.

See also : Conversion, Overflow

Upstream, downstream

GRAFCET

Before and after, in the reading direction of the GRAFCET (top to bottom). The upstream step precedes a transition, the downstream step follows it.

See also : Evolution

Variable

General concepts

A named piece of data handled by the program: an input, an output or an internal memory. A logic variable is TRUE or FALSE (1 or 0).

Studomate declares variables in the variables table, shared between GRAFCET, Ladder and HMI.

See also : Mnemonic, Input, Output

Wiring: normally open (NO) and normally closed (NC)

General concepts

Also called : NO, NC, normally open, normally closed

The way a button or sensor is connected. Wired normally open (NO), it is 0 at rest and 1 when operated; wired normally closed (NC), it is 1 at rest and 0 when operated.

The physical wiring and the contact chosen in the program are two different things.

See also : Contact, Input, Push button
